intro.en: Linear regression is usually the first supervised learning algorithm students meet. It predicts a number (such as a house price or an exam score) from one or more input features by fitting a straight line (or a flat plane) through the data.
intro.ru: Linear regression aam taur par pehla supervised learning algorithm hota hai jo students seekhte hain. Yeh ek ya zyada input features se koi number predict karta hai (maslan ghar ki qeemat ya exam ke marks), data ke beech mein ek seedhi line (ya plane) fit kar ke.

definition.en: Linear regression models the output as a weighted sum of the inputs plus a bias, y = w x + b, and chooses w and b so that the mean squared error between predictions and true values is as small as possible.
definition.ru: Linear regression output ko inputs ke weighted sum aur bias ke taur par dekhta hai, y = w x + b, aur w aur b aise chunta hai ke predictions aur asal values ke darmiyan mean squared error sab se kam ho.

explanation.en: Each training example gives an error (residual): the vertical distance between the true value and the line. Squaring the residuals makes them positive and punishes large errors more. The best line is the one with the smallest average squared error. For one feature there is a closed-form solution: the slope is the covariance of x and y divided by the variance of x, and the intercept makes the line pass through the point (mean of x, mean of y). With many features we use the normal equation or gradient descent. The slope tells you how much y changes when x increases by one unit. R squared tells you what fraction of the variation in y the line explains (1 is perfect, 0 means no better than predicting the mean).
explanation.ru: Har training example ka ek error (residual) hota hai: asal value aur line ke darmiyan khara (vertical) faasla. Residuals ko square karne se woh positive ho jate hain aur bare errors ki saza zyada hoti hai. Behtareen line woh hai jis ka average squared error sab se kam ho. Ek feature ke liye seedha formula maujood hai: slope = x aur y ki covariance / x ki variance, aur intercept aisa hota hai ke line (x ka mean, y ka mean) wale point se guzre. Zyada features ke liye normal equation ya gradient descent istemal hota hai. Slope batata hai ke x mein 1 unit izafe se y kitna badalta hai. R squared batata hai ke y ki variation ka kitna hissa line samjha pati hai (1 matlab perfect, 0 matlab mean predict karne se behtar nahi).

example.en: Study hours x = [1, 2, 3, 4] and marks y = [2, 4, 5, 8]. Mean x = 2.5, mean y = 4.75. Covariance sum: (-1.5)(-2.75) + (-0.5)(-0.75) + (0.5)(0.25) + (1.5)(3.25) = 4.125 + 0.375 + 0.125 + 4.875 = 9.5. Variance sum: 2.25 + 0.25 + 0.25 + 2.25 = 5. Slope w = 9.5 / 5 = 1.9. Intercept b = 4.75 - 1.9 x 2.5 = 0. So marks = 1.9 x hours. A student who studies 5 hours is predicted to get 9.5 marks.
example.ru: Parhai ke ghante x = [1, 2, 3, 4] aur marks y = [2, 4, 5, 8]. x ka mean = 2.5, y ka mean = 4.75. Covariance ka sum: (-1.5)(-2.75) + (-0.5)(-0.75) + (0.5)(0.25) + (1.5)(3.25) = 9.5. Variance ka sum: 2.25 + 0.25 + 0.25 + 2.25 = 5. Slope w = 9.5 / 5 = 1.9. Intercept b = 4.75 - 1.9 x 2.5 = 0. Yaani marks = 1.9 x ghante. Jo student 5 ghante parhe us ke 9.5 marks predict honge.

intro.en: Despite its name, logistic regression is a classification algorithm. It predicts the probability that an example belongs to the positive class, for example whether an email is spam.
intro.ru: Naam ke bawajood logistic regression classification ka algorithm hai. Yeh predict karta hai ke koi example positive class mein hone ka kitna imkan (probability) hai, maslan email spam hai ya nahi.

definition.en: Logistic regression computes a linear score z = w . x + b and passes it through the sigmoid function to get a probability p = 1 / (1 + e^-z). The class is positive when p is at least a threshold, usually 0.5.
definition.ru: Logistic regression pehle linear score z = w . x + b nikalta hai aur phir sigmoid function se probability p = 1 / (1 + e^-z) banata hai. Agar p threshold (aam taur par 0.5) ya us se zyada ho to class positive hoti hai.

explanation.en: The sigmoid squeezes any real number into the range 0 to 1, so the output can be read as a probability. The decision boundary is where p = 0.5, which is where z = 0: a straight line (or plane) in feature space, so logistic regression is a linear classifier. The weights are learned by minimising the log loss (binary cross-entropy), which strongly punishes confident wrong predictions. There is no closed-form solution, so gradient descent or a similar optimiser is used. A positive weight means that increasing the feature increases the probability of the positive class.
explanation.ru: Sigmoid kisi bhi number ko 0 aur 1 ke darmiyan le aata hai, is liye output ko probability samjha ja sakta hai. Decision boundary wahan hai jahan p = 0.5, yaani z = 0: feature space mein ek seedhi line (ya plane), is liye logistic regression linear classifier hai. Weights log loss (binary cross-entropy) kam kar ke seekhe jate hain, jo pakke yaqeen wali ghalat predictions ki bari saza deta hai. Iska seedha formula nahi, is liye gradient descent jaisa optimiser lagta hai. Positive weight ka matlab hai ke feature barhne se positive class ki probability barhti hai.

example.en: Suppose a trained model has w = 2 and b = -4 for one feature (hours studied) and predicts pass/fail. For 3 hours: z = 2 x 3 - 4 = 2, p = 1 / (1 + e^-2) = 0.881, so the student is predicted to pass. For 1 hour: z = -2, p = 0.119, predicted fail. The boundary is at z = 0, i.e. 2 hours.
example.ru: Farz karein ek trained model mein ek feature (parhai ke ghante) ke liye w = 2 aur b = -4 hai aur yeh pass/fail predict karta hai. 3 ghante: z = 2 x 3 - 4 = 2, p = 1 / (1 + e^-2) = 0.881, yaani pass. 1 ghanta: z = -2, p = 0.119, yaani fail. Boundary z = 0 par hai, yaani 2 ghante.

intro.en: A decision tree makes predictions by asking a sequence of yes/no questions about the features, like a flowchart. It is easy to read and explain, which makes it popular in practice.
intro.ru: Decision tree features ke baare mein haan/nahi wale sawalon ka silsila pooch kar prediction karta hai, bilkul flowchart ki tarah. Ise parhna aur samjhana asaan hai, is liye yeh bohat istemal hota hai.

definition.en: A decision tree recursively splits the data on the feature and threshold that make the child nodes as pure as possible (lowest Gini impurity or entropy). Leaves hold the predicted class (or value).
definition.ru: Decision tree data ko baar baar us feature aur threshold par taqseem karta hai jis se bachay (child) nodes sab se zyada khalis (pure) hon, yaani Gini impurity ya entropy sab se kam ho. Leaves mein predicted class (ya value) hoti hai.

explanation.en: At each node the algorithm tries every feature and candidate threshold, measures the impurity of the two resulting groups, and keeps the split with the biggest impurity decrease (information gain). Gini impurity is 1 minus the sum of squared class proportions: 0 for a pure node, 0.5 for a 50/50 binary node. Entropy is -sum p log2 p: 0 for pure, 1 for 50/50. Splitting stops at a maximum depth, a minimum number of samples, or when nodes are pure. Deep trees memorise the training data (overfitting), so depth limits or pruning are important.
explanation.ru: Har node par algorithm har feature aur har mumkin threshold azmata hai, do banne wale groups ki impurity naapta hai, aur woh split rakhta hai jis se impurity sab se zyada kam ho (information gain). Gini impurity = 1 - classes ke hisson ke squares ka sum: pure node ke liye 0, binary 50/50 ke liye 0.5. Entropy = -sum p log2 p: pure ke liye 0, 50/50 ke liye 1. Splitting maximum depth, kam az kam samples, ya pure nodes par ruk jati hai. Bohat gehre trees training data ratt lete hain (overfitting), is liye depth ki had ya pruning zaroori hai.

example.en: A node has 6 'yes' and 4 'no' examples: Gini = 1 - (0.6^2 + 0.4^2) = 1 - 0.52 = 0.48. A split gives left = 5 yes / 1 no and right = 1 yes / 3 no. Gini left = 1 - (0.833^2 + 0.167^2) = 0.278; Gini right = 1 - (0.25^2 + 0.75^2) = 0.375. Weighted = 0.6 x 0.278 + 0.4 x 0.375 = 0.317. The impurity drops from 0.48 to 0.317, a gain of 0.163.
example.ru: Ek node mein 6 'haan' aur 4 'nahi' hain: Gini = 1 - (0.6^2 + 0.4^2) = 0.48. Ek split se left = 5 haan / 1 nahi aur right = 1 haan / 3 nahi. Left ka Gini = 0.278; right ka Gini = 0.375. Weighted = 0.6 x 0.278 + 0.4 x 0.375 = 0.317. Impurity 0.48 se 0.317 ho gayi, yaani 0.163 ka gain.

intro.en: KNN is one of the simplest ML algorithms: to classify a new point, look at the k closest training points and take a vote.
intro.ru: KNN sab se aasaan ML algorithms mein se hai: naye point ki class janne ke liye k sab se qareebi training points dekhein aur vote lein.

definition.en: K-Nearest Neighbors predicts the label of a new example from the labels of the k training examples closest to it (usually by Euclidean distance): majority vote for classification, average for regression.
definition.ru: K-Nearest Neighbors naye example ka label un k training examples ke labels se predict karta hai jo us ke sab se qareeb hon (aam taur par Euclidean distance se): classification mein majority vote, regression mein average.

explanation.en: KNN is a lazy learner: training just stores the data, and all the work happens at prediction time. The choice of k controls the bias-variance trade-off: k = 1 follows every noisy point (high variance), a large k smooths too much (high bias). An odd k avoids ties in binary problems. Because it relies on distances, features must be on similar scales, so standardise them first. Prediction is slow for large datasets because the distance to every training point is computed, unless an index such as a KD-tree is used.
explanation.ru: KNN lazy learner hai: training mein sirf data save hota hai aur saara kaam prediction ke waqt hota hai. k ka intikhab bias-variance trade-off tay karta hai: k = 1 har noisy point ke peeche jata hai (high variance), bohat bara k cheezon ko zyada hamwar kar deta hai (high bias). Binary masail mein taaq (odd) k se tie nahi hota. Yeh distance par chalta hai, is liye features ka scale milta julta hona chahiye, pehle standardise karein. Bare datasets par prediction dheemi hoti hai kyunki har training point tak distance nikalta hai, jab tak KD-tree jaisa index na ho.

example.en: Training points: A(1,1) red, B(2,1) red, C(4,4) blue, D(5,4) blue, E(4,5) blue. New point P(2,2). Distances: A = sqrt(1+1) = 1.41, B = sqrt(0+1) = 1, C = sqrt(4+4) = 2.83, D = sqrt(9+4) = 3.61, E = sqrt(4+9) = 3.61. With k = 3 the neighbours are B, A, C: two red, one blue, so P is red.

intro.en: Naive Bayes is a fast probabilistic classifier based on Bayes' theorem. It works surprisingly well for text problems such as spam filtering.
intro.ru: Naive Bayes Bayes' theorem par mabni ek tez probabilistic classifier hai. Yeh text ke masail jaise spam filtering mein heraan kun had tak acha kaam karta hai.

definition.en: Naive Bayes chooses the class c that maximises P(c) x P(x1 | c) x P(x2 | c) x ..., assuming the features are conditionally independent given the class (the 'naive' assumption).
definition.ru: Naive Bayes woh class c chunta hai jis ke liye P(c) x P(x1 | c) x P(x2 | c) x ... sab se zyada ho, yeh farz kar ke ke class maloom ho to features ek doosre se azad hain (yahi 'naive' assumption hai).

explanation.en: Bayes' theorem turns 'how likely are these features for each class' into 'how likely is each class given these features'. The prior P(c) is the share of each class in the training data. The likelihoods P(xi | c) are estimated per feature: counts for categorical/word features (Multinomial NB) or a normal distribution with the class mean and variance for numeric features (Gaussian NB). Because the evidence P(x) is the same for all classes, we only compare the numerators. Laplace smoothing adds 1 to counts so that an unseen word does not make a probability zero. In practice log-probabilities are added instead of multiplying tiny numbers.
explanation.ru: Bayes' theorem 'har class mein yeh features kitne mumkin hain' ko 'in features ke saath har class kitni mumkin hai' mein badal deta hai. Prior P(c) training data mein har class ka hissa hai. Likelihoods P(xi | c) har feature ke liye nikalte hain: categorical/words ke liye ginti (Multinomial NB) ya numeric features ke liye class ke mean aur variance wali normal distribution (Gaussian NB). Evidence P(x) har class ke liye barabar hai, is liye sirf numerators ka muqabla hota hai. Laplace smoothing ginti mein 1 jama karti hai taake koi na dekha hua lafz probability ko zero na kar de. Amal mein bohat chhote numbers zarab karne ki jagah log-probabilities jama ki jati hain.

example.en: Spam filter: P(spam) = 0.4, P(ham) = 0.6. P('free' | spam) = 0.5, P('free' | ham) = 0.1. For an email containing 'free': spam score = 0.4 x 0.5 = 0.20, ham score = 0.6 x 0.1 = 0.06. Normalising: P(spam | 'free') = 0.20 / 0.26 = 0.769, so the email is classified as spam.

intro.en: A Support Vector Machine finds the boundary that separates two classes with the widest possible safety gap (margin). With kernels it can also draw curved boundaries.
intro.ru: Support Vector Machine woh boundary dhoondti hai jo do classes ko sab se chaure hifazati faasle (margin) ke saath alag kare. Kernels ke saath yeh murhi hui boundaries bhi bana sakti hai.

definition.en: An SVM is a classifier that chooses the hyperplane w . x + b = 0 with the maximum margin between the classes; the training points that touch the margin are called support vectors.
definition.ru: SVM ek classifier hai jo woh hyperplane w . x + b = 0 chunta hai jis ka classes ke darmiyan margin sab se zyada ho; jo training points margin ko chhoote hain unhein support vectors kehte hain.

explanation.en: Many lines can separate two groups, but the one with the widest margin usually generalises best. The margin width is 2 / ||w||, so maximising it means minimising ||w|| while every point stays on the correct side. Only the support vectors determine the boundary; moving other points does not change it. Real data overlaps, so the soft-margin SVM allows some violations, controlled by C: a large C punishes violations heavily (narrow margin, risk of overfitting), a small C allows more violations (wider margin). The kernel trick (RBF, polynomial) computes similarities in a higher-dimensional space without building it, which gives non-linear boundaries.
explanation.ru: Do groups ko bohat si lines alag kar sakti hain, lekin sab se chaure margin wali aam taur par naye data par behtar chalti hai. Margin ki chaurai 2 / ||w|| hai, is liye ise barhane ka matlab ||w|| ko kam karna hai jabke har point sahi taraf rahe. Sirf support vectors boundary tay karte hain; baqi points hilane se boundary nahi badalti. Asal data aapas mein mila hota hai, is liye soft-margin SVM kuch khilaf warziyon ki ijazat deti hai, jinhein C control karta hai: bara C sakht saza (patla margin, overfitting ka khatra), chhota C zyada narmi (chaura margin). Kernel trick (RBF, polynomial) zyada dimensions wali space ko banaye baghair similarities nikalta hai, jis se non-linear boundaries banti hain.

example.en: Suppose a trained linear SVM has w = (1, 1) and b = -3. For the point (2, 2): w . x + b = 2 + 2 - 3 = 1 > 0, so it is in the positive class (and exactly on the margin). For (1, 1): 1 + 1 - 3 = -1, negative class (also on the margin). The margin width is 2 / ||w|| = 2 / sqrt(2) = 1.414.
example.ru: Farz karein trained linear SVM mein w = (1, 1) aur b = -3 hai. Point (2, 2): w . x + b = 2 + 2 - 3 = 1 > 0, yaani positive class (aur bilkul margin par). (1, 1): 1 + 1 - 3 = -1, negative class (yeh bhi margin par). Margin ki chaurai 2 / ||w|| = 2 / sqrt(2) = 1.414.

subject: Machine Learning

intro.en: K-Means is the classic unsupervised learning algorithm. It groups unlabeled data into k clusters of similar points, for example grouping customers by shopping behaviour.
intro.ru: K-Means unsupervised learning ka classic algorithm hai. Yeh be-label data ko k milte julte points ke groups (clusters) mein baant deta hai, maslan customers ko shopping ke andaaz se groups mein.

definition.en: K-Means partitions the data into k clusters by repeatedly assigning each point to the nearest centroid and moving each centroid to the mean of its assigned points, until the assignments stop changing.
definition.ru: K-Means data ko k clusters mein baantta hai: baar baar har point ko qareebi centroid ko dena, aur har centroid ko us ke points ke mean par le jana, jab tak assignments badalna band na ho jayein.

explanation.en: The algorithm minimises the within-cluster sum of squares (inertia): the total squared distance of points to their centroid. Each step (assign, then update) can only lower inertia, so it always converges, but possibly to a local minimum that depends on the starting centroids - that is why k-means++ initialisation and several restarts are used. You must choose k yourself; the elbow method plots inertia against k and looks for the bend, and the silhouette score measures how well separated the clusters are. K-Means assumes roughly round clusters of similar size and is sensitive to feature scale and outliers.
explanation.ru: Algorithm within-cluster sum of squares (inertia) kam karta hai: points ka apne centroid tak kul squared faasla. Har step (assign, phir update) inertia ko sirf kam kar sakta hai, is liye yeh hamesha converge hota hai, lekin shuruati centroids ke hisaab se local minimum par bhi ruk sakta hai - isi liye k-means++ aur kai dafa dobara chalana istemal hota hai. k aap ko khud chunna hota hai; elbow method k ke muqable inertia ka graph bana kar mor (bend) dhoondta hai, aur silhouette score batata hai ke clusters kitne alag hain. K-Means golai wale aur milte julte size ke clusters farz karta hai aur feature scale aur outliers se asar leta hai.

example.en: Points 1, 2, 3, 10, 11, 12 on a line with k = 2 and starting centroids 1 and 2. Step 1: 1 goes to centroid 1; 2, 3, 10, 11, 12 go to centroid 2. Update: c1 = 1, c2 = (2+3+10+11+12)/5 = 7.6. Step 2: 1, 2, 3 are closer to 1; 10, 11, 12 closer to 7.6. Update: c1 = 2, c2 = 11. subject: Machine Learning

intro.en: Gradient descent is the optimisation method behind most of machine learning: it trains linear and logistic regression, neural networks and more by walking downhill on the loss function.
intro.ru: Gradient descent zyada tar machine learning ke peeche ka optimisation method hai: yeh loss function par neeche ki taraf chal kar linear aur logistic regression, neural networks waghera train karta hai.

definition.en: Gradient descent minimises a function by repeatedly moving the parameters a small step in the direction opposite to the gradient: theta := theta - alpha x gradient, where alpha is the learning rate.
definition.ru: Gradient descent kisi function ko kam karta hai: baar baar parameters ko gradient ki ulti taraf ek chhota qadam le ja kar: theta := theta - alpha x gradient, jahan alpha learning rate hai.

explanation.en: The gradient points in the direction of steepest increase, so the negative gradient points downhill. Each update reduces the loss if the learning rate is small enough. A learning rate that is too large overshoots and can diverge; one that is too small makes training slow. Batch gradient descent uses all data per step; stochastic gradient descent (SGD) uses one example and mini-batch uses a small group, which is faster and noisier. For convex losses (linear regression MSE) gradient descent reaches the global minimum; for non-convex losses (neural networks) it can stop in a local minimum or saddle point. Feature scaling makes the loss surface rounder and speeds up convergence.
explanation.ru: Gradient sab se tez barhne ki simt batata hai, is liye manfi (negative) gradient neeche ki taraf hota hai. Learning rate kaafi chhota ho to har update loss kam karta hai. Bohat bara learning rate minimum se aage nikal jata hai aur diverge ho sakta hai; bohat chhota training ko dheema kar deta hai. Batch gradient descent har qadam par saara data, stochastic gradient descent (SGD) ek example, aur mini-batch chhota group istemal karta hai, jo tez lekin zyada noisy hai. Convex loss (linear regression ka MSE) par gradient descent global minimum tak pohanchta hai; non-convex (neural networks) par local minimum ya saddle point par ruk sakta hai. Feature scaling loss surface ko gol bana kar convergence tez karti hai.

example.en: Minimise f(x) = x^2 starting at x = 4 with learning rate 0.1. Gradient f'(x) = 2x. Step 1: x = 4 - 0.1 x 8 = 3.2. Step 2: x = 3.2 - 0.1 x 6.4 = 2.56. Step 3: x = 2.048. Each step multiplies x by 0.8, so x moves steadily towards the minimum at 0. With learning rate 1.1 the factor becomes 1 - 2.2 = -1.2, so |x| grows and the method diverges.
example.ru: f(x) = x^2 ko x = 4 se learning rate 0.1 ke saath kam karein. Gradient f'(x) = 2x. Step 1: x = 4 - 0.1 x 8 = 3.2. Step 2: x = 3.2 - 0.1 x 6.4 = 2.56. Step 3: x = 2.048. Har step x ko 0.8 se zarab karta hai, is liye x minimum (0) ki taraf barhta hai. Learning rate 1.1 par factor 1 - 2.2 = -1.2 ho jata hai, |x| barhta hai aur method diverge ho jata hai.
